quotes: Drupal 8 and later versions can be configured to use Symfony's trusted host mechanism to prevent HTTP Host header spoofing. To enable the trusted host mechanism, you enable the allowed hosts setting

authority.summary: Drupal's installation documentation states that the trusted host mechanism is enabled through this settings key and describes the response when a request's Host header does not match.

context_requirements.subject: config_sync_directory
context_requirements.why_it_matters: Settings files can include further settings files that this analysis does not follow, so a declaration made in an included file would not have been seen.

finding.assertion: No trusted_host_patterns declaration was observed in the settings files read.

conclusion.candidate: No trusted host declaration was observed in the files read; an included settings file could still declare one.
conclusion.confirmed: No trusted host declaration was observed, and the documentation states this mechanism is what prevents Host header spoofing.
conclusion.unknown: Whether the setting is declared could not be established.

finding.evidence_explanation: The settings-declaration evidence contains no trusted_host_patterns entry.
finding.human_title: Trusted host patterns were not observed
limitations: Included settings files are not followed, so this is not a claim about effective runtime settings.
No hostname is recorded by this analysis.

remediation.guidance: Confirm whether $settings['trusted_host_patterns'] is declared, including in any included settings file, and declare it if it is not.

review.authority: reviewed against the pinned trusted host settings snapshot

scope.notes: The Symfony trusted host mechanism is used from Drupal 8 onwards.

summary: Drupal's trusted host mechanism is enabled by declaring $settings['trusted_host_patterns']. No such declaration was observed in the settings files this analysis read.
title: Trusted host patterns are not declared in the observed settings file
